questions.question: At railroad crossings, bus drivers must:

options.text: Not stop, but slow down to 25 mph below the speed limit.
Not stop, but open the door to listen for trains.
Stop and check for approaching trains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and check for approaching trains.
questions.explanation: When driving a bus near railroad tracks, you must stop 15 to 50 feet from the nearest track. Look and listen for trains. Only move forward when you are sure no trains are coming. You do not need to stop at streetcar crossings, when a police officer is directing traffic, when the traffic signal is green, or at crossings marked "exempt" or "abandoned."

questions.question: If your engine catches fire, you should not:

options.text: Turn off the engine as soon as possible.
Spray foam from under the vehicle.

questions.explanation: In an engine fire, turn off the engine right away. Do not open the hood if you can help it. Spray foam through the louvers or from underneath the vehicle.

questions.question: To leave a parking space safely, you should park:

options.text: So you must back up to leave.
So you can drive forward to leave.
On the side of a road, not in a lot.

questions.correctAnswerText: So you can drive forward to leave.
questions.explanation: Backing up is dangerous, so avoid it when you can. Park so you can drive forward to exit your space.

questions.question: After you stop during the stop/start test, you should:

options.text: Not use four-way flashers because it is a test, not an emergency.
Leave the vehicle in first gear.
Park in front of a fire hydrant.

questions.explanation: When you stop during the stop/start test, turn on your four-way flashers and shift into neutral or park. Do not block driveways, intersections, fire hydrants, or signs.

questions.question: When stopping, you should:

options.text: Press the brake pedal down slowly.
Press the brake pedal down quickly.
Pump the brake pedal, but do not hold it down.
Use the same brake force every time you stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the brake pedal down slowly.
questions.explanation: Press the brake pedal smoothly and gradually every time you slow or stop. The amount of brake pressure you need depends on your speed and how quickly you need to stop.

questions.question: Backing with a trailer is dangerous because:

options.text: You cannot see behind the vehicle.
Most trucks cannot move in reverse.
Cargo may fall out of the trailer.
There may be extra weight in the front of the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see behind the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Backing is dangerous because you cannot see everything behind your vehicle. If you must back up, use a helper if possible.

questions.question: Engine belts should be:
questions.explanation: Check engine belts for tightness and wear. The right amount of slack varies by engine, so learn what is correct for your vehicle.

questions.question: During the on-road driving test, you must do all of the following except:

options.text: Complete the test without a moving violation.
Obey traffic signs and signals only when other traffic is present.

questions.correctAnswerText: Obey traffic signs and signals only when other traffic is present.
questions.explanation: You must drive safely and responsibly during the on-road test. This means wearing your safety belt, obeying all traffic signs and signals at all times, following all traffic laws, and avoiding accidents and moving violations.

questions.question: Leaking shock absorbers:
questions.explanation: The suspension system holds the axles in place. Damaged suspension parts, such as leaking shock absorbers, are potentially dangerous defects.

questions.question: When changing lanes:

options.text: You do not need a turn signal.

questions.explanation: Change lanes slowly and smoothly to keep control of your vehicle. This also gives other drivers time to move out of your way if you did not see them. Always use a turn signal.

questions.question: During the basic vehicle control skills test, what is a pull-up?

options.text: A pull-up always counts against the applicant.
A pull-up should be completed at least once.
Stopping without changing direction is not considered a pull-up.
Excessive pull-ups are acceptable in the opinions of some test administrators.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stopping without changing direction is not considered a pull-up.
questions.explanation: A pull-up happens when you stop and then move forward to get a better position. Just stopping without moving forward is not a pull-up. Too many pull-ups will be counted as errors.

questions.question: If you hear or feel something unusual while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Hope the vehicle lasts until someone else drives it.

questions.explanation: If you see, hear, smell, or feel anything unusual while driving, you should stop right away and check what is causing it.

questions.question: If you double your speed from 20 mph to 40 mph, how does it affect your braking distance?
questions.explanation: When you double your speed, your braking distance increases four times. Going from 20 to 40 mph means your vehicle needs four times as much distance to stop.

questions.question: Before driving in winter, you should check:
questions.explanation: Before winter driving, check your heating and defrosting systems, coolant and antifreeze levels, wipers and washers, tire tread, tire chains, lights, and exhaust system. Clear all ice and snow from windows, mirrors, and steps.

questions.question: What does an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) do?

options.text: Allow you to drive faster than normal.
Allow you to follow other vehicles more closely.
Allow you to drive less carefully.
It does not reduce your stopping distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: It does not reduce your stopping distance.
questions.explanation: ABS helps you keep control when you brake hard. However, it does not necessarily make your stopping distance shorter.

questions.question: What does an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) do?

options.text: Allow the rear wheels to lock up.
Allow all wheels to lock up.
Alert other drivers when you are braking.

questions.explanation: ABS prevents your wheels from locking up when you brake hard on slippery surfaces.

questions.question: After you start the engine, when should oil pressure reach normal level?
questions.explanation: Watch your gauges after starting the engine. Oil pressure should reach normal level within a few seconds.

questions.question: What affects your stopping distance the most?
questions.explanation: The faster you drive, the longer your stopping distance will be.

questions.question: During a basic vehicle control skills test, what is an encroachment?

options.text: The vehicle crossing over an exercise boundary line.
A driver completing a single pull-up.
A driver putting the vehicle in neutral and applying the parking brake.
The vehicle stalling while shifting gears.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle crossing over an exercise boundary line.
questions.explanation: An encroachment is when any part of your vehicle touches or crosses a boundary line. Every encroachment counts as an error.

questions.question: How many classes of hazardous materials are there?
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials are divided into nine classes based on the type of risk they pose.
